name: Apollo–Soyuz Test Project
achieved: Apollo and Soyuz docked in orbit on 17 July 1975, and two days of joint operations followed in the first joint US–Soviet space mission.
caveat: Rooted in the 1972 US–USSR space cooperation agreement.

name: Shuttle–Mir Program
achieved: Seven American astronauts lived aboard Mir alongside Russian cosmonauts, spending nearly 1,000 days in orbit during Phase 1 of the ISS programme (1994–1998).
caveat: Phase 1 of the ISS programme; included the 1997 Mir fire and Progress collision.

name: International Space Station
achieved: Five space agencies (NASA, Roscosmos, ESA, JAXA, CSA) run the station, which has been visited by astronauts from 18 countries.
caveat: 1998 IGA signed by US, Russia, Japan, Canada and 11 ESA states. China is excluded by US law (2011 Wolf Amendment). Russia committed through 2028; deorbit planned around 2030. 'Continuously crewed since Nov 2000' was not stated on the NASA page.

name: ESA Rosetta comet mission
achieved: Rosetta launched on 2 March 2004, reached comet 67P in August 2014, delivered the Philae lander to its surface (a historic first) on 12 November 2014, and ended with a controlled impact on the comet on 30 September 2016.
caveat: ESA-led. The ESA fact sheet does not mention NASA's instrument contributions (Alice, MIRO, IES), so US membership rests on general knowledge.

name: Long Now Rosetta Project – Rosetta Disk flown on ESA's Rosetta
achieved: A 7.5 cm nickel disk, micro-etched with about 7,000 pages of language material covering 1,000 languages and assembled by the Long Now Foundation, was attached to ESA's Rosetta orbiter before its 2004 launch and rode with the spacecraft to comet 67P.
caveat: Likely the 'Rosetta stone project for the whole earth'. It is a private initiative of the US-based Long Now Foundation, not an intergovernmental programme; ESA carried the disk. ESA gives 1,000 languages; the ~7,000 pages figure is from Long Now's archived page (ESA gives no page count). The later 2008 Rosetta Disk is reported to cover about 1,500 languages (not verified).

name: ITER fusion project
achieved: Seven Members (China, EU, India, Japan, Korea, Russia, US) share construction mainly through in-kind components, with Europe covering about 45.6% and each other Member 9.1%.
caveat: Other member: Korea. ITER page notes Switzerland participates via Fusion for Energy from 1 Jan 2026 and the UK has discontinued participation. Non-member cooperation: Australia, Kazakhstan, Canada. Agreement signed Nov 2006 (date not stated on fetched page). 2024 baseline: research operations ~2034.

name: CERN Large Hadron Collider
achieved: The LHC experiments ATLAS and CMS announced the discovery of the Higgs boson on 4 July 2012.
src: CERN (Higgs page; Council decision on Russia/Belarus at home.cern/news/news/cern/cern-council-decides-conclude-cooperation-russia-and-belarus-2024)
caveat: LHC approved 1994, first beam 2008. India associate member since 2017; US and Japan observers/major contributors; China participates via institutes only. CERN Council decided on 15 Dec 2023 to end cooperation agreements with Belarus (27 June 2024) and Russia (30 Nov 2024).

name: International Human Genome Project
achieved: Twenty centres in six countries (US, UK, Japan, France, Germany, China) completed the reference human genome in 2003, with China sequencing about 1% (on chromosome 3).
caveat: NHGRI confirms 20 centres in the US, UK, France, Germany, Japan and China and the Oct 1990-Apr 2003 span. China's 1% share (about 30 Mb on chromosome 3, approved 8 Jul 1999, only developing-country participant) is from a Science and Technology Daily article republished on ncsti.gov.cn (https://www.ncsti.gov.cn/kjdt/ztbd/swyy/xwdt/202102/t20210210_26604.html).

name: Event Horizon Telescope
achieved: On 10 April 2019 more than 200 researchers using a global array of eight radio telescopes published the first image of a black hole (M87*).
caveat: Partners include the East Asian Observatory (representing China, Japan, Korea, Taiwan and others), ASIAA, KASI and NINS, plus European and Mexican institutes. No Chinese institute is named individually. Sgr A* image 2022 (not on fetched page).

name: LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA gravitational-wave network
achieved: The LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA fourth observing run began on 24 May 2023 and was extended to 18 November 2025, with Virgo (Italy) and KAGRA (Japan) operating alongside the two US LIGO detectors.
caveat: The first detection (GW150914) and GW170817 are well known but are not on the fetched page. India's role: the Government of India approved LIGO-India at Rs 2600 crore with DAE as lead agency (PIB, 10 Aug 2023: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1947441&reg=48&lang=2); it is not yet an operating detector.

name: Daya Bay Reactor Neutrino Experiment
achieved: Daya Bay made the first definitive measurement of the neutrino mixing angle θ13 in 2012 and ended operations on 12 December 2020, with 237 participants from 41 institutions.
caveat: Collaborators: China, US, Czech Republic, Russia, Chile, plus significant contributions from Taiwan and Hong Kong. 'others' = Chile.

name: Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO)
achieved: JUNO began physics data-taking on 26 August 2025, and its first results (19 November 2025) measured the solar oscillation parameters θ12 and Δm²21 with 1.6× better precision than all previous experiments combined.
caveat: China-led (IHEP). More than 700 scientists from 74 institutions in 17 countries and regions; JINR (Dubna, Russia-hosted) contributed a 50-person team. Civil construction began in 2015.

name: Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer (AMS-02) on the ISS
achieved: Delivered to the ISS by the Space Shuttle in 2011, AMS-02 is run by a team of 56 institutes from 16 countries, including the US, European states, China, Russia and Taiwan.
caveat: DOE-sponsored and led by Samuel Ting. NASA confirms launch on STS-134 on 16 May 2011 and installation on 19 May 2011 (https://www.nasa.gov/alpha-magnetic-spectrometer/about-alpha-magnetic-spectrometer/). NASA's page gives 44 institutions, the ESA page 56 institutes from 16 countries.

name: Chang'e-4 far-side landing: international payloads and NASA coordination
achieved: After Chang'e-4 made the first soft landing on the lunar far side on 3 January 2019, NASA and CNSA discussed using LRO's LAMP instrument to look for the landing plume, LRO imaged the landing site, and the two agencies agreed to share significant findings at UN COPUOS in February 2019.
caveat: Data coordination, not a joint mission. CNSA confirms payloads from the Netherlands, Germany, Sweden and Saudi Arabia, a Chinese-Russian radioisotope heat source, and LRO scientists' cooperation (https://www.cnsa.gov.cn/english/n6465719/c6805233/content.html). The 30 Jan 2019 LRO image is on NASA's 'First Look' page. Replaces the Scientific American source.

name: Chang'e-6 lunar far-side sample return with foreign payloads
achieved: Chang'e-6, which landed its return capsule in Inner Mongolia on 25 June 2024 with the first lunar far-side samples, carried an ESA negative-ion analyser, a French radon detector, an Italian laser retroreflector and a Pakistani cubesat.
caveat: 'others' = Pakistan. The commonly cited 1,935.3 g sample mass was not on the fetched page and has been removed.

name: SKA Observatory
achieved: The SKA Observatory, created in early 2021, had 12 member states by November 2024 after India joined in July 2024 by signing and ratifying the SKAO Convention.
caveat: Members include Australia, South Africa, UK, China, Italy, Netherlands, Portugal, Switzerland, Spain and others. The full list and the SKA-Low first image (Mar 2025) were not on the fetched page.

name: Argo profiling float array
achieved: By its 20th anniversary in January 2019, Argo's array of about 4,000 floats had collected 2 million ocean profiles, with 26 countries deploying around 800 floats a year.
caveat: Coordinated by IOC/WMO. National Argo programmes in the US, Europe, UK, Japan, China and India (and Russia) are listed by the Argo programme office (https://argo.ucsd.edu/links/).

name: MOSAiC Arctic drift expedition
achieved: The 389-day expedition drew more than 80 institutes from 20 countries and seven icebreakers and research vessels, including Akademik Fedorov, Kapitan Dranitsyn, Admiral Makarov and Akademik Tryoshnikov.
caveat: Led by AWI (Germany). The factsheet does not state ship nationalities (the four named are Russian vessels) and lists no Chinese icebreaker. China took part through ten institutes, including the Polar Research Institute of China; Russia through AARI and Rosmorport; the US and UK through NOAA, NASA, NSF, BAS, NERC and others (partner list: https://mosaic-expedition.org/team/partner-institutions/).

name: International Geophysical Year
achieved: Scientists in 67 nations took part between 1 July 1957 and 31 December 1958; the US Explorer 1 (IGY contribution) discovered the Van Allen radiation belts, and the USSR launched Sputnik 3 as a scientific satellite.
caveat: The PRC withdrew in 1957 over Taiwan's participation (general knowledge; not on the NASA page). IGY led to the 1959 Antarctic Treaty.

name: Belle II experiment at SuperKEKB
achieved: Belle II at Japan's SuperKEKB collider brings together more than 1,000 physicists from more than 26 countries, including 16 US institutions.
caveat: Start year 2019 (physics run) is not on the fetched page. Participation of Chinese, Indian and Russian institutes is not verified on that page. Belle II's institute list (belle2.org institutional map) loads via JavaScript and could not be read.

name: Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA)
achieved: ALMA on Chile's Chajnantor plateau is funded 37.5% by ESO, 37.5% by North America (US, Canada, Taiwan) and 25% by East Asia (Japan, Taiwan, Korea), with 66 antennas contributed by the three partners.
caveat: 'others' = Canada, Korea, Chile (Taiwan not counted). The UK is included via ESO membership.

name: FAIR – Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research
achieved: Nine shareholder countries (Finland, France, Germany, India, Poland, Romania, Russia, Slovenia, Sweden) signed the FAIR convention on 4 October 2010; the UK is associated and Czechia is an aspirant partner.
caveat: FAIR still lists Russia as a shareholder; reports say its cooperation has been frozen since 2022, but the fetched page does not confirm this.

name: Einstein Probe X-ray mission
achieved: CAS's Einstein Probe launched on 9 January 2024 with ESA, Germany's MPE and France's CNES as partners; ESA helped build and calibrate X-ray instruments in exchange for 10% of the data.

name: SVOM gamma-ray burst satellite (China–France)
achieved: SVOM, a French–Chinese gamma-ray-burst mission of CNSA, CAS, CNRS and CEA, launched on a Long March 2C on 22 June 2024 into a 625 km orbit.
caveat: Preceded by the China–France CFOSAT ocean satellite (2018).

name: ESA (and NASA) tracking support for Chandrayaan-3
achieved: ESA's Kourou station and the UK's Goonhilly station, together with NASA's Deep Space Network, tracked Chandrayaan-3, which landed on the Moon on 23 August 2023.
caveat: A service arrangement, not a joint mission.

name: WHO Intensified Smallpox Eradication Programme
achieved: WHO's intensified eradication plan, launched in 1967, ended with eradication certified in December 1979 and declared in 1980.
caveat: The USSR's vaccine donations and the US CDC's role are well documented but not on the fetched WHO page. Japan's Isao Arita later led the programme. The PRC was outside WHO until 1972.

name: Sabin oral polio vaccine trials in the USSR
achieved: After Soviet virologists Chumakov and Smorodintsev worked with Sabin from 1956, his oral vaccine was given to millions of Soviet children (77 million people in the USSR during 1959-1961), and the campaign's results led to licensure of the oral vaccine in the US in 1961.
caveat: The 1956 State Department-facilitated contact between Sabin, Chumakov and Smorodintsev is from Hotez, PLoS Negl Trop Dis 2017 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5444589/). Replaces the Gulf News source.

name: Global Polio Eradication Initiative
achieved: Since GPEI was set up in 1988, polio incidence worldwide has fallen by about 99%, and wild poliovirus now circulates in only two countries.
caveat: Partners: WHO, Rotary, US CDC, UNICEF, Gates Foundation, Gavi. The two endemic countries (Pakistan, Afghanistan) are not named on the fetched page.

name: 2014–2016 West Africa Ebola response
achieved: The outbreak infected more than 28,600 people and killed 11,325 before it was declared over in June 2016; China sent a 163-member PLA team to run a 100-bed Ebola hospital in Monrovia, alongside other national deployments.
caveat: These were parallel national deployments (US Operation United Assistance in Liberia, UK in Sierra Leone, France in Guinea) under UN/WHO coordination. The WHO page names no partners.

name: Rapid SARS-CoV-2 genome sharing
achieved: China publicly shared the genetic sequence of SARS-CoV-2 on 12 January 2020, giving laboratories worldwide the basis for developing diagnostic tests.
caveat: The WHO timeline does not give the 11 Jan virological.org posting (see https://virological.org/t/novel-2019-coronavirus-genome/319) or the first PCR protocol date. How quickly data were shared remains disputed.

name: COVAX vaccine facility
achieved: COVAX delivered nearly 2 billion COVID-19 vaccine doses to 146 economies before closing on 31 December 2023.
caveat: China joined in October 2020 and the US in 2021 as the largest donor. India's Serum Institute was a key supplier, but India's 2021 export halt cut deliveries.

name: WHO Pandemic Agreement
achieved: The World Health Assembly adopted the WHO Pandemic Agreement on 20 May 2025; it will open for signature once a pathogen access and benefit-sharing annex is adopted.
caveat: As of July 2026 annex negotiations were still continuing (extended on 1 May 2026). The US did not take part (withdrawal from WHO announced Jan 2025; not on the WHO page). Russia's position was not verified.

name: Megatons to Megawatts (US–Russia HEU Purchase Agreement)
achieved: By December 2013, 500 metric tons of Russian HEU, equivalent to 20,000 warheads, had been down-blended into US reactor fuel that supplied nearly 10% of all US electricity over the previous fifteen years.
caveat: The 10% figure is the commonly cited average share over the programme's life; Centrus/USEC was the US executive agent.

name: Nunn–Lugar Cooperative Threat Reduction in Russia/former USSR
achieved: The Cooperative Threat Reduction programme has deactivated more than 7,500 nuclear warheads in the former Soviet Union and helped states such as Kazakhstan, Ukraine and Belarus.
caveat: The DTRA page says 'more than 7,500' and does not give a scorecard figure such as 7,599. It does not mention Russia ending cooperation (umbrella agreement lapsed 2013, Russia projects ended about 2014; general knowledge). The DTRA page and congress.gov CRS report R43143 returned 403 to automated fetches this session, so the 7,500 figure was not re-read.

name: INF Treaty eliminations
achieved: The US and USSR destroyed a combined 2,692 short-, medium- and intermediate-range missiles by the treaty's 1 June 1991 deadline.
caveat: The US withdrew on 2 August 2019. The source (Arms Control Association) is an NGO, not a government page; the earlier per-side split was removed because the source does not give it.

name: Joint Verification Experiment
achieved: US and Soviet scientists jointly monitored nuclear tests at the Nevada Test Site (Kearsarge, 17 August 1988) and Semipalatinsk (September 1988), building the confidence that made possible ratification of the Threshold Test Ban Treaty in 1990.

name: Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (Iran nuclear deal)
achieved: On 28 December 2015 more than 11 tonnes (25,000 lb) of Iran's low-enriched uranium materials were shipped to Russia, and in April 2017 China's CNNC signed the first contract to redesign Iran's Arak heavy-water reactor.
src: World Nuclear News (2015 shipment; 2017 Arak contract)
caveat: 'others' = Iran. The US withdrew in May 2018. The E3 triggered snapback in 2025 and UN sanctions were reimposed in September 2025; Russia and China dispute that this was lawful.

name: Removal and destruction of Syria's declared chemical weapons
achieved: All 600 metric tonnes of Syria's Priority 1 chemicals were transloaded at Gioia Tauro, Italy, onto the US vessel Cape Ray in July 2014 for neutralisation at sea, which finished ahead of schedule by August 2014.
caveat: The White House thanked Denmark, Norway, Italy, Finland, Germany and the UK for key contributions and Russia and China for assistance. Russian/Chinese naval escorts were widely reported but are not confirmed on these two pages. 'others' = Norway, Syria. OPCW later found undeclared stocks and use.

name: CTBTO International Monitoring System
achieved: The IMS, planned as 337 facilities in 89 countries and about 90% operational, detected all six of North Korea's declared nuclear tests (2006–2017).
caveat: The treaty is not in force. The US and China signed but have not ratified. Russia withdrew its ratification in 2023 but remains a signatory. India has not signed.

name: P5 leaders' statement on preventing nuclear war
achieved: On 3 January 2022 China, France, Russia, the UK and the US jointly affirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.
caveat: Product of the P5 Process (since 2009). EU here means France.

name: Montreal Protocol on ozone-depleting substances
achieved: Nearly 99% of banned ozone-depleting substances have been phased out, and the January 2023 assessment projects ozone recovery to 1980 levels by about 2066 over Antarctica, 2045 over the Arctic and 2040 elsewhere.
caveat: Universal ratification (2009, first UN treaty to achieve it) is well documented but was not shown on the fetched ozone.unep.org page.

name: US–China Joint Announcement on Climate Change → Paris Agreement
achieved: On 11–12 November 2014 the US announced a target of 26–28% below 2005 emissions by 2025, and China announced it would peak CO2 around 2030 and reach about 20% non-fossil energy by 2030.
caveat: The US left Paris in 2020, rejoined in 2021 and withdrew again with effect from January 2026.

name: Antarctic Treaty
achieved: Signed in Washington on 1 December 1959 by the 12 IGY nations, the treaty reserves Antarctica for peaceful purposes and freezes territorial claims, and it now has 58 Parties.
caveat: The NSF URL redirects here. China and India acceded in 1983 (not on page).

name: Agreement to Prevent Unregulated High Seas Fisheries in the Central Arctic Ocean
achieved: The EU and nine countries (Canada, China, Denmark, Iceland, Japan, Korea, Norway, Russia, US) brought a precautionary ban on unregulated high-seas fishing into force on 25 June 2021, initially for 16 years until 2037.
caveat: Signed in October 2018 with an initial 16-year term. 'others' = Canada, Denmark (for Greenland and the Faroes), Iceland, Korea, Norway.

name: Cospas-Sarsat satellite search-and-rescue system
achieved: Founded by Canada, France, Russia and the USA, the system had 42 participants and had supported the rescue of more than 37,000 people from 1982 to 2013.
caveat: 'others' = Canada (founders only). Later lives-saved totals are not on this 2015 overview.

name: WMO World Weather Watch global data exchange
achieved: In October 2021 the Extraordinary World Meteorological Congress approved a Unified Data Policy that reaffirms the free and unrestricted exchange of weather, climate and related Earth-system data among WMO's 193 Members.
caveat: World Weather Watch has existed since 1963 (not on the cited page). The June 2021 Executive Council endorsement is on https://wmo.int/node/14000.

name: High Seas Treaty (BBNJ Agreement)
achieved: Adopted in June 2023, the agreement passed 60 ratifications when Morocco became the 60th party in September 2025, and it entered into force on 17 January 2026.
caveat: Members listed are signatories; not all have ratified (the US has not). Russia did not join the consensus.

name: Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework
achieved: Under China's COP15 presidency, the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework was adopted in Montreal on 19 December 2022.
caveat: The 30x30 target is part of the framework but not mentioned on the fetched page. The US is not a CBD party.

name: Counter-piracy off Somalia (SHADE coordination)
achieved: SHADE, chaired in rotation by EU NAVFOR, NATO and CMF, drew about 120 government, industry and military representatives in 2016 to deconflict counter-piracy operations, with China, Russia and India among the 'independent deployers'.
caveat: Coordination only, not a joint command. Japan joined CMF's CTF151 in 2013 per the Cabinet Secretariat's 2025 counter-piracy report (https://www.cas.go.jp/jp/gaiyou/jimu/pdf/siryou2/counter-piracy2025.pdf); the forum's 2008 founding and piracy statistics are not on the fetched pages. Piracy resurged in 2023-24.

name: MH370 surface search, southern Indian Ocean
achieved: In March 2014, aircraft and ships from Australia, New Zealand, the US, China, Japan, Korea and Malaysia searched hundreds of thousands of square kilometres of the southern Indian Ocean, but no sighted object was confirmed as from MH370.
caveat: 'others' = Australia, New Zealand, Korea, Malaysia. The AMSA-coordinated surface phase moved to JACC on 31 March 2014. The later underwater search (suspended Jan 2017) and private searches are not covered by this page. UK/India/EU roles are not listed there and were removed.

name: Tham Luang cave rescue
achieved: Experts from the US (about 40 INDOPACOM personnel), UK diving teams, six Chinese cave-rescue experts and Japanese JICA drainage advisers joined Thai forces in the 8–10 July 2018 rescue, during which one retired Thai Navy SEAL died.
src: The Nation (Thailand); US Air Force 353rd SOW
caveat: 'others' = Myanmar, Laos (per The Nation); Australia also took part (not in the fetched sources). Domain 'health' is used because no humanitarian or rescue category exists. US Air Force: www.353sow.af.mil/News/Article/2268380/thai-cave-rescue-two-years-later. The 353rd SOW page did not respond to automated fetches, and no PRC MFA or UK government page detailing the teams was found.

name: Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank
achieved: AIIB has grown to 111 approved members, starting from 57 prospective founding members confirmed in April 2015 that included the UK, Germany, France, India and Russia.
caveat: The US and Japan declined to join. Founding-member details come from Nippon.com because the AIIB member table did not render.

name: New Development Bank (BRICS)
achieved: Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa signed the NDB Agreement in Fortaleza on 15 July 2014; the bank has since added Bangladesh, the UAE, Egypt and Algeria.
caveat: 'others' = Brazil, South Africa, Bangladesh, UAE, Egypt, Algeria. Later members and the 2015 opening are not on the fetched MFA page.

name: G20 Debt Service Suspension Initiative
achieved: From May 2020 to December 2021 the initiative suspended about US$12.9 billion in debt-service payments for 48 of 73 eligible countries.
caveat: Private creditors largely stayed out. Followed by the G20 Common Framework.

name: Bletchley Declaration on AI safety
achieved: On 1 November 2023 the declaration was issued by 28 countries and the EU, including the US, China, India and Japan, on the risks and safe development of frontier AI.
caveat: Not binding. Russia did not take part. New Zealand joined on 23 October 2024.
